text: Before the war Bakhmut was a salt-and-gypsum city of about 70–75,000 people on the Bakhmutka river.
Bakhmut lay at the junction of the roads from Sloviansk (M03), Siversk (T0513) and Kostiantynivka (T0504).
From early July 2022 Russia relied on the Wagner Group to carry the attack on Bakhmut.
Wagner began recruiting in Russian prisons on 1 July 2022 and enlisted at least 48,000 convicts before the scheme ended in February 2023.
From August 2022 Wagner threw its convicts at Bakhmut's eastern and southern edges in small assault groups, with executions for retreat.
Through the autumn of 2022 the front at Bakhmut barely moved; Prigozhin's own figure for Wagner's advance was 100–200 m a day.
Bakhmut became a symbol; Zelensky visited on 20 December 2022 and took the defenders' flag to the US Congress the next day.
In January 2023 Wagner, joined by VDV and other regular troops, took Soledar to the north-east of Bakhmut (12–16 January).
After Soledar, Wagner swung round Bakhmut's north (Krasna Hora, Paraskoviivka, Berkhivka, Yahidne) and south (Klishchiivka, Ivanivske) in early 2023.
Ukraine debated withdrawing from Bakhmut, and the US advised it to.
In early March 2023 Ukraine gave up the east bank of the Bakhmutka but chose to reinforce the rest of Bakhmut.
Wagner took Bakhmut block by block: the AZOM plant about 28 March 2023, the city hall on 2 April, and about 76% of the city by 11 April.

text: Prigozhin fought the Russian MoD in public over shells, and on 5 May 2023 threatened to leave Bakhmut.
From 9 May 2023 Ukrainian brigades counterattacked the weak Russian regulars on Bakhmut's flanks.
Wagner took the last western blocks of Bakhmut anyway, and on 20 May 2023 Prigozhin declared the city captured.
Wagner handed Bakhmut over to the army from 25 May 2023 and mutinied a month later.
Bakhmut held for about ten months and then fell (chapter window to 20 May 2023).
From August to December 2022 the front stayed on Bakhmut's eastern and southern outskirts.
Soledar fell on 12–16 January 2023; Ukraine confirmed the withdrawal on 25 January.
The northern and southern Russian pincers closed to the Bakhmut city edge in February 2023.
Ukraine gave up the east bank of the Bakhmutka by 7 March 2023, leaving Russia with at least 50% of Bakhmut.

text: The AZOM plant in Bakhmut fell about 28 March 2023 and the city hall on 2 April.
By 11 April 2023 Russia held at least 76.5% (30.68 km²) of Bakhmut.
By 18 May 2023 Russia held over 95% of Bakhmut.
Prigozhin declared Bakhmut taken on 20 May 2023.
A Ukrainian foothold in Bakhmut's south-western outskirts, the "Airplane" area by the MiG-17 monument, stayed in Ukrainian hands into June 2023.
Russia never closed the Bakhmut pocket: the western roads came under fire from February 2023 but were never cut.
Ukrainian counterattacks on Bakhmut's flanks from 9 May 2023 retook about 17–20 km² within a week, but not the city.
By 10 July 2023 Ukrainian flank counterattacks at Bakhmut had retaken 24 km².
Wagner handed over its Bakhmut positions between 25 May and 5 June 2023.
Wagner mutinied on 23–24 June 2023.
ISW judged that Wagner had shown signs from late December 2022 that it could not fight beyond Bakhmut.
Leaked Wagner records counted by Mediazona and BBC Russian give 19,547 Wagner dead (15 July 2022 – 6 June 2023): 17,175 convicts and 2,372 contract fighters.
RUSI uses the same figure of 19,547 Wagner dead at Bakhmut.
Zelensky put Wagner's losses at 21,000 killed and 60,000–80,000 wounded.
Meduza and Mediazona estimate all Russian dead at Bakhmut and Soledar at about 21,000, in a range of 19,100–25,250.

text: Wagner's first prison recruitment took place at IK-7 Yablonevka on 1 July 2022.
The first Wagner convict recruit died on 15 July 2022, the start date of Wagner's own death records.
After Lysychansk fell, Russia turned on Bakhmut on 4 July 2022.
ISW counts Russia's whole gain in the Bakhmut area from 4 July 2022 to mid-February 2023 at about 500 km².
On 1 August 2022 Russian ground assaults south and south-east of Bakhmut failed, and attacks on Soledar (13 km north-east) and Yakovlivka were repelled.
On 4 August 2022 Russia attacked near Bakhmut in five to seven strike groups.
On 4 August 2022 Ukrainian troops pulled back from Semihirya and Dolomitne towards Kodema.
The 93rd Mechanised Brigade arrived in the Bakhmut sector on 11 August 2022.
On 13–25 August 2022 fighting reached the Knauf gypsum plant on Soledar's edge.
In August 2022 Russian sources claimed a foothold on Bakhmut's north-eastern outskirts; the claim was unconfirmed.
In August 2022 Wagner and the LNR 6th Cossack Regiment attacked around Bakhmut and Soledar.
On 6 September 2022 Russia claimed Kodema, 13 km south-east of Bakhmut.
By 20 September 2022 Wagner was recruiting directly in Russian prisons.
On 22 September 2022, at about 11:00, the central bridge over the Bakhmutka was destroyed, cutting off the east bank of Bakhmut.
On 26 September 2022 Zelensky thanked the 93rd and 10th Mountain Assault Brigades for the Bakhmut direction.
In October 2022 Prigozhin said Wagner was advancing 100–200 m a day at Bakhmut.
Prigozhin later claimed that he and Surovikin planned "Operation Bakhmut Meatgrinder" in October 2022.
On 8 November 2022 Russian forces attacked Bakhmut itself and Opytne, Ivanhrad and Klishchiivka.
On 8 November 2022 Cherevatyi said Wagner made up most of the attackers at Bakhmut.
By 29 November 2022 Russia had made marginal gains at Bakhmut, slower than its sources claimed.
Named Wagner dead reached 3,605 by 29 November 2022.
On 10 December 2022 Zelensky called Bakhmut "burnt ruins"; about 12,000 civilians remained, in basements.
On 20 December 2022 Zelensky visited frontline positions on Bakhmut's approaches and handed out awards, under the slogan "#bakhmutfortress".
On 21 December 2022 Zelensky gave the US Congress a flag signed by Bakhmut's defenders.
By 26 December 2022 more than 60% of Bakhmut's infrastructure was damaged or destroyed, with 225 shellings in a day.
On 27 December 2022 ISW assessed that Russia might be nearing culmination at Bakhmut and was down to squad-sized assault groups.
In late December 2022 Wagner turned on Soledar and took most of Bakhmutske.
On 31 December 2022 Prigozhin said every house in Bakhmut was a "fortress", with Ukrainian lines "every 10 meters".
On 4–7 January 2023 the battle for Soledar intensified: a Wagner fighter was filmed at the Artemsil plant while Ukrainians held the salt mine.
By 7 January 2023 Wagner had entered Klishchiivka.
On 10–11 January 2023 Wagner reached central and western Soledar and cut its supply roads.
Gerasimov became Russian theatre commander on 11 January 2023.
12 January 2023 was Wagner's deadliest day, with 213 named dead.

On 13 January 2023 the Russian MoD announced Soledar taken "on the evening of January 12" without naming Wagner, then credited Wagner six hours later.
Wagner took Sil station north-west of Soledar on 16 January 2023.
Prigozhin claimed Klishchiivka on 19 January 2023, and the Russian MoD on 20 January.
On 25 January 2023 Cherevatyi confirmed the withdrawal from Soledar "to save the lives of the personnel", without encirclement.

On 4–8 February 2023 Russia advanced at Krasna Hora, Zaliznianske, the Stupky area and Ivanivske, coming within 2.5 km of the M03.
Wagner's last prison recruitment took place on 7 February 2023.
On 9 February 2023 Prigozhin said: "We have completely discontinued the recruitment of prisoners".

On 11 February 2023 the T0504 bridge over the canal west of Ivanivske was found destroyed.
Paraskoviivka fell on 17–19 February 2023: Prigozhin claimed it on 17 February, and the flag removal was filmed on 19 February.
On 20 February 2023 Zelensky said Ukraine would defend Bakhmut, but "not at any cost".
On 21 February 2023 Prigozhin accused the Russian MoD of "treason" over shells.
On 22 February 2023 Prigozhin posted a photo of dozens of dead Wagner fighters.
The Russian MoD called Prigozhin's shell claims "completely untrue".
On 22–27 February 2023 Wagner fought into Berkhivka and Yahidne and threatened the Khromove road.
Cherevatyi counted 32 Russian attacks around Bakhmut and 14 inside it on 26 February 2023.
On 3–4 March 2023 Ukraine blew the Bakhmutka bridge in the north-east of Bakhmut and the bridge on the Khromove road.

text: On 3–4 March 2023 Prigozhin said one road into Bakhmut was left.
In early March 2023 about 4,000 civilians remained in Bakhmut, which had lost 95% of its people.
On 6 March 2023 Zaluzhnyi and Syrskyi recommended holding Bakhmut, and Zelensky ordered reinforcements.
On 6 March 2023 Austin said a withdrawal from Bakhmut would be no "significant strategic setback".
On 6 March 2023 Wagner's flag went up at the T-34 monument in eastern Bakhmut.
On 7–8 March 2023 a controlled Ukrainian withdrawal left everything east of the Bakhmutka.
On 8 March 2023 ISW assessed that Russia held at least 50% of Bakhmut.
On 9–10 March 2023 the MiG-17 monument in Bakhmut was blown up.
By 10 March 2023 Wagner was within 800 m of AZOM.
On 13 March 2023 Prigozhin said "550 attempts" to get ammunition had been ignored.
On 13 March 2023 Syrskyi told the Washington Post: "We need to buy time".
On 15 March 2023 the Stavka met and decided: "Reinforce this sector and inflict maximum possible damage".

text: On 19–20 March 2023 a Ukrainian counterattack pushed Russians off the T0504 south-west of Ivanivske.
On 20 March 2023 Prigozhin claimed 70% of Bakhmut.
Wagner took the AZOM complex about 28 March 2023.
On the night of 2 April 2023 Prigozhin raised a flag at the Bakhmut city administration and said the city was "legally" taken.

On 20–21 April 2023 Wagner took the Bakhmut-2 station.
On 20–21 April 2023 Russian milbloggers claimed 83% of Bakhmut.
On 26 April 2023 Russians reached Persha Lisova St near the Yuvileina road out to Khromove.
On 26 April 2023 Ukraine bombed high-rises in Bakhmut with JDAMs.
On 1 May 2023 Kirby said Russia had suffered about 20,000 killed and 80,000 wounded since December, nearly half the dead Wagner.
On 4–5 May 2023 Prigozhin stood among corpses and said Wagner would leave Bakhmut on 10 May unless supplied.
On 9 May 2023 Prigozhin stayed in Bakhmut and accused the 72nd Motor Rifle Brigade of abandoning a flank position.
On 9–11 May 2023 the 3rd Assault Brigade broke the Russian 72nd Motor Rifle Brigade south-west of Bakhmut.
On 11 May 2023 Syrskyi said Russians had retreated up to 2 km near Bakhmut.
On 12–16 May 2023 Ukrainian counterattacks hit north-west of Bakhmut (Berkhivka reservoir) and south-west.
Cherevatyi said Ukraine retook 17.3 km² near Bakhmut in three days in May 2023.
Maliar said Ukraine retook about 20 km² near Bakhmut in mid-May 2023.
On 17–18 May 2023 Russia held over 95% of Bakhmut.
On 18 May 2023 Prigozhin said Ukraine held 1.28 km² of Bakhmut and admitted the flanks were lost.
On 20 May 2023 Prigozhin declared Bakhmut fully captured, at the last high-rise near the MiG-17 monument.
On 20 May 2023 Maliar said Ukrainians still held the "Airplane" area in Bakhmut.
On the evening of 20 May 2023 the Russian MoD announced the "liberation of Artyomovsk" by Wagner with army support.
On the night of 20–21 May 2023 Putin congratulated Wagner's assault groups and the units that covered the flanks at Bakhmut.
On 21 May 2023 Wagner flags went up over the westernmost block of Bakhmut.
On 21 May 2023 Zelensky said at Hiroshima that Bakhmut was "only in our hearts".
On 21 May 2023 Biden said Russians had suffered "over 100,000 casualties" at Bakhmut.
On 24 May 2023 Prigozhin said more than 20,000 Wagner fighters had died, about half of them convicts.
From 25 May to 5 June 2023 Wagner handed Bakhmut over to Russian MoD and DNR units; about 90 Wagner fighters were left on 1 June.
On 1 June 2023 Maliar said Ukraine still held Bakhmut's south-western outskirts.
On 10 June 2023 the Russian MoD ordered volunteer units onto contracts by 1 July, and Prigozhin refused.
On 23–24 June 2023 Wagner mutinied, took Rostov and got to about 200 km from Moscow.
On 3–10 July 2023 the largest Ukrainian gains near Bakhmut were near Klishchiivka, across the canal.
By 10 July 2023 Ukraine claimed fire control over Bakhmut and 24 km² retaken since the counteroffensive began.
On 24 July 2023 Maliar said Ukraine had retaken 4 km² near Bakhmut in a week.
On 25 July 2023 the Ukrainian General Staff said Russians pulled back from positions in Andriivka.
On 14–15 September 2023 the 3rd Assault Brigade retook Andriivka.
On 17–18 September 2023 Klishchiivka was liberated.
On 18 September 2023 Syrskyi said the Bakhmut–Horlivka line was breached and three Russian brigades had lost combat capability.

The 2023 Ukrainian flank counterattacks at Bakhmut stayed within about 10 km of the city.
ISW counted only about 500 km² gained by Russia in the whole Bakhmut area from 4 July 2022 to mid-February 2023.
By ISW's terrain count the city of Bakhmut is about 40 km²: 30.68 km² was 76.5% of it on 11 April 2023.

Ukraine kept fighting for the roads west of Bakhmut; ISW credits this with forcing "Wagner forces into urban warfare and grinding directly through the city itself".

cites.quote: Wagner forces into urban warfare and grinding directly through the city itself

text: Prigozhin had offered on 3 March 2023 to let Zelensky withdraw from Bakhmut.
Decision point (Russia, March–April 2023): the Russian MoD and Prigozhin agreed on 11 April 2023 that Wagner was the main effort inside Bakhmut, with the VDV on the flanks.
ISW read the Wagner-in-the-city, VDV-on-the-flanks split as a way to take Bakhmut "while minimizing casualties among conventional Russian forces".

cites.quote: while minimizing casualties among conventional Russian forces

text: Prigozhin complained that Bakhmut's flanks were held only by "irregular and degraded units"; that weakness is what the May 2023 counterattacks exploited.
Prigozhin claimed "550 attempts" to get ammunition, all ignored.
On 4–5 May 2023 Prigozhin set the 10 May deadline to leave Bakhmut, and on 7 May he announced an MoD promise of supplies.
On 9 May 2023 Prigozhin stayed at Bakhmut, saying the MoD had threatened him with treason.
ISW judged that the Russian MoD had deprioritised Bakhmut to prepare for Ukraine's counteroffensive.
Decision point (Ukraine, from 9 May 2023): Cherevatyi said the aim was "to destroy Russian concentration areas and encircle the city, not to conduct frontal assaults".

cites.quote: to destroy Russian concentration areas and encircle the city, not to conduct frontal assaults

text: Syrskyi called the May 2023 flank counterattacks at Bakhmut "active defense".
After the May 2023 flank counterattacks about 17–20 km² was retaken in a week, but Bakhmut still fell on 20 May.
Maliar said Russia had to commit "most of their reserves" to the Bakhmut area.
Decision point (Russia, 20 May – 5 June 2023): Prigozhin announced the handover of Bakhmut for 25 May and a two-month rest from 1 June.
ISW called Wagner's withdrawal from Bakhmut "strategically questionable" on the eve of the counteroffensive.
DNR and regular Russian units took over Bakhmut from Wagner.
Kofman and Lee saw the Bakhmut flank as the first axis of the 2023 Ukrainian offensive, which drew in most of Russia's VDV.
RUSI says reinforcing the Bakhmut flank in summer 2023 reflected "strong political direction to demonstrate progress" and that it "devolved into fights for treelines".

cites.quote: strong political direction to demonstrate progress

text: After the summer 2023 flank attacks Andriivka and Klishchiivka were retaken in September, but not Bakhmut.
Prigozhin said at noon on 20 May 2023: "Bakhmut was completely taken … from house to house"; Cherevatyi replied: "This is not true".

cites.quote: Bakhmut was completely taken … from house to house

text: The Kyiv Independent says Prigozhin's 20 May 2023 capture video was filmed about 3 km from the fighting.

observations.subject: Prigozhin's video location from the fighting

text: On the evening of 20 May 2023 the Russian MoD said the "liberation of Artyomovsk has been completed" by Wagner, supported by Southern Group artillery and aviation.

cites.quote: liberation of Artyomovsk has been completed

text: Overnight on 20–21 May 2023 Putin congratulated "Wagner's assault groups" and the army units "who provided … cover on their flanks", promising state awards.
Russian state television said the "unassailable fortress" myth of Bakhmut was "crushed", comparing the capture to Berlin in 1945 and talking of an open road to Kramatorsk and Dnipro.
The Russian MoD's first Soledar announcement left Wagner out, and a second six hours later credited "volunteers of assault detachments".
Putin then credited the Russian MoD and the General Staff for Soledar.
Zelensky said the Russians were "fighting among themselves over who should be credited" for Soledar.

cites.quote: fighting among themselves over who should be credited

text: In February 2023 the Russian MoD again called Wagner only "volunteers of assault detachments" over Paraskoviivka, and Prigozhin said the MoD was "spitting at" Wagner.
Bloomberg's sources said the Russian MoD would not let Prigozhin take credit for Bakhmut on state media.
Prigozhin said the "Bakhmut meat grinder" was planned with Surovikin in October 2022 to draw in and exhaust the Ukrainian army, not to take the city.
At the turn of 2022–23 Prigozhin admitted Wagner could not break through at Bakhmut.
Prigozhin accused the Russian MoD of "treason" over shells and published photos and videos of his dead.
Prigozhin claimed Ukraine had 200,000 reserves ready to strike.
Late in May 2023 Prigozhin warned of "a revolution, just like in 1917".
A leaked US document said Prigozhin had offered to give Ukrainian intelligence Russian positions in exchange for a Ukrainian withdrawal; he denied it.
Prigozhin claimed 11,000 Ukrainians were killed at Bakhmut in February 2023.
Prigozhin claimed 50,000 Ukrainian dead over the Bakhmut battle.
The Russian MoD claimed 700 Ukrainians killed in three days at Soledar.
Russia also claimed 220 Ukrainians killed at Bakhmut in one day in March 2023.
Against Russian claims of Ukrainian losses, the UALosses name counts for Bakhmut are 4,557–5,501.
Pushilin said taking Bakhmut would open the way to Kramatorsk and Sloviansk.
Shoigu made the same claim, that taking Bakhmut would open the way further, on 7 March 2023, and Prigozhin rejected it.
ISW judged Russia had no reserve to exploit the capture of Bakhmut.
Two former Wagner fighters said they had been ordered to kill civilians in Soledar and Bakhmut, including children.
Ukraine's prosecutor opened a case over Prigozhin's removal of families with children from Bakhmut.
The defector Andrey Medvedev publicised Wagner's brutal disciplinary practices.
RUSI says Russia "traded lives for time" at Bakhmut while it built its southern defences.
ISW said Prigozhin's final blocks in Bakhmut were "purely symbolic".
Western officials called Bakhmut "quite a small tactical event" with "a unique opportunity to kill a lot of Russians".

cites.quote: a unique opportunity to kill a lot of Russians

counter: Wagner convict assault waves (small groups, executions for retreat, veterans consolidating behind)
measure: Ukrainian positional defence of Bakhmut in house strongpoints
effect: slow, costly erosion of the defence: about 30 m per wave, city taken block by block
rationale: Waves of small convict groups take up to 80% losses, but each group of about 10 moves about 30 m and digs in for the next to pass through, so Wagner took Bakhmut block by block while trained Wagner losses stayed low (88% of its dead were convicts).

counter: Ukrainian artillery shortage against a 5:1 Russian artillery advantage
measure: Ukrainian attritional defence of Bakhmut (holding the city to bleed Russian forces)
effect: degrades the exchange ratio; Ukrainians "pay with our lives for the lack of ammunition"
rationale: With Ukrainian batteries cut from 150 full loads a day to 30 and Russia holding a 5:1 artillery advantage, Russian artillery controlled the supply roads from February 2023 and RUSI judges losses then turned unfavourable; Kofman and Lee said the exchange was "not nearly as favorable as it was before".

counter: Ukrainian flank counterattacks (active defence against Russian concentrations)
measure: Russian northern and southern pincers aimed at encircling Bakhmut
effect: prevents encirclement and pushes the flanks back, but does not save the city
rationale: Counterattacks on the T0504 in March and on the weak regular-held flanks from 9 May 2023 retook about 17–20 km² in a week; Prigozhin admitted the flanks were lost and that he could no longer encircle anything, and the pocket was never closed.
